lessons.title: Understand Absolute Value of Rational Numbers
lessons.objective: I can find the absolute value of a rational number — an integer, fraction, or decimal — as its distance from zero.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain absolute value using the words distance, zero, opposite, and rational number.

concept.heading: What is absolute value?
concept.intro: An integer is a whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero. The absolute value of a number is how far it is from zero on the number line. Distance is never negative.
concept.keyIdea: Absolute Value. Formula: |a| = Distance of a from 0 (always ≥ 0). 1. Absolute value represents distance on a number line, never direction. 2. Distance is always positive or zero: |-7| = 7 and |7| = 7. 3. Context: Magnitude of temperature, debt, elevation regardless of sign

worked.title: Watch me
lines: I want to find the absolute value of -6, written |-6|.
I find -6 on the number line. It sits 6 steps to the left of zero.
Distance does not care about direction, so -6 is 6 units from zero.
So |-6| = 6. Even though -6 is negative, its absolute value is positive 6.
linesEs: Quiero hallar el valor absoluto de -6, escrito |-6|.
Hallo el -6 en la recta numérica. Está 6 pasos a la izquierda del cero.
A la distancia no le importa la dirección, así que -6 está a 6 unidades del cero.
Entonces |-6| = 6. Aunque -6 es negativo, su valor absoluto es 6 positivo.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now let's find |3|. Where is 3 on the number line? It is 3 steps to the right of zero.
How far is it from zero? It is 3 units away.
linesEs: Ahora hallemos |3|. ¿Dónde está el 3 en la recta numérica? Está 3 pasos a la derecha del cero.
¿Qué tan lejos está del cero? Está a 3 unidades.

vocabulary.definition: A number smaller than zero, to the left of zero on a number line.

lessons.title: Compare and Order Integers and Rational Numbers
lessons.objective: I can compare and order integers using a number line.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words compare, order, greater than, and less than.

concept.heading: How do you compare and order integers?
concept.intro: To compare integers means to see which one is greater or less. On a number line, numbers get bigger as you go right and smaller as you go left.
concept.keyIdea: Comparing & Ordering Rational Numbers. Formula: Left is Less (<) | Right is Greater (>). 1. Plot or visualize numbers on a horizontal number line. 2. Numbers further to the left are always less than numbers to the right. 3. For negatives: A negative number with a larger absolute value is smaller (-10 < -2)

worked.title: Watch me
lines: I will compare -7 and -5. They are both negative, so I look at the number line.
-7 is 7 steps left of zero. -5 is only 5 steps left of zero.
-7 is farther to the left, so -7 is the smaller number.
I write -7 < -5. The open side of the symbol points to the bigger number, -5.
linesEs: Voy a comparar -7 y -5. Los dos son negativos, así que miro la recta numérica.
El -7 está 7 pasos a la izquierda del cero. El -5 está solo 5 pasos a la izquierda del cero.
El -7 está más a la izquierda, así que -7 es el número menor.
Escribo -7 < -5. El lado abierto del símbolo apunta al número mayor, -5.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now let's compare -2 and 3. Which one is to the left on the number line? The -2 is left of zero.
Which one is to the right? The 3 is right of zero.
So which is greater, and what symbol do we use? 3 is greater, so -2 < 3.
linesEs: Ahora comparemos -2 y 3. ¿Cuál está a la izquierda en la recta numérica? El -2 está a la izquierda del cero.
¿Cuál está a la derecha? El 3 está a la derecha del cero.
Entonces ¿cuál es mayor y qué símbolo usamos? El 3 es mayor, así que -2 < 3.

vocabulary.definition: Use a number line to decide which integers are greater or less and place them in order.
A straight line where numbers are placed in order; numbers get smaller to the left and larger to the right.
To see if a number is bigger, smaller, or equal to another.
vocabulary.example: -3 < 2 because -3 is farther left on the number line than 2

vocabulary.definition: To arrange numbers by size, from least to greatest or greatest to least.
vocabulary.example: Least to greatest: -5, -2, 0, 3, 7 (left to right on the number line)

vocabulary.definition: The > sign, showing one number is bigger.
vocabulary.example: 4 > -1 because 4 is to the right of -1 on the number line

vocabulary.definition: The < sign, showing one number is smaller.
vocabulary.example: -6 < -2 because -6 is farther left — it is farther from zero

vocabulary.definition: A whole number smaller than zero, like -5.
vocabulary.example: -4 is 4 units to the LEFT of zero on the number line

vocabulary.definition: Whole numbers and their opposites, like -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
A statement that uses < or > to compare two numbers.

support.prompt: What is the absolute value of -9?
support.explanation: Absolute value is the distance from zero. -9 is 9 units from zero, so |-9| = 9.
feedback: That is what you get if you got the sign backwards. Instead: Absolute value is the distance from zero.
0 would only be the answer if the number were zero. Count how many units sit between -9 and 0 on the number line.
The 1 doesn't come from measuring the distance. Absolute value counts the units from zero to the number, whatever the sign.
hints: Absolute value asks: how FAR is -9 from zero? It's about distance, not direction.
Picture -9 on a number line and count the hops back to 0. A distance is never negative.
Start at -9 and count the steps to reach 0: 1, 2, 3, ... How many hops does it take in all?

support.prompt: Which integer has the GREATEST absolute value: -3, 7, -5, 2?
feedback: |-5| = 5 is a big distance, but one option sits even farther from zero. Distance ignores the sign — measure every number before deciding.
|-3| = 3, one of the shortest distances in the list. Compare the distances from zero, not the signs.
|2| = 2, the smallest distance of all. Find each number's absolute value, then compare them.
hints: 'Greatest absolute value' means farthest from zero — the sign doesn't matter.
Find each number's distance from 0: |-3|, |7|, |-5|, |2|. Then pick the biggest distance.
Start with |-3| = 3 and |-5| = 5. Now find the distances for 7 and 2 and compare all four.

support.explanation: Zero is 0 units from itself on the number line, so |0| = 0.
feedback: Absolute value is distance from zero, not a change to the digit.
An absolute value can never be negative, because a distance is never negative.
There is an answer: zero has an absolute value too. Ask yourself how far zero is from itself.
hints: Absolute value = distance from zero. Here the number inside the bars IS zero.
Ask: how many units do you travel from 0 to reach 0 on the number line?
Place your finger on 0. Count the hops needed to get to 0 — that count is the value of |0|.

core.prompt: Which statement about absolute value is TRUE?
choices: |-4| = |4| because both are 4 units from zero
core.explanation: Absolute value measures distance from zero. Both -4 and 4 are 4 units from zero, so |-4| = |4| = 4.
feedback: Not quite. Absolute value measures distance from zero.
Negatives don't cancel inside the absolute value bars. Count the units from zero to -4.
Being positive doesn't change the distance. Measure how many units each number is from zero before you compare.
hints: Remember the definition: absolute value measures DISTANCE from zero, and a distance is never negative.
Test each statement against the definition. Ask: how far is -4 from zero? How far is 4? Can distance be negative?
First count -4's units from zero, then count 4's units from zero. Compare the two counts before judging.

core.prompt: Which number has the LEAST absolute value: −1.5, 0.75, −1/4, or 2?
core.explanation: |−1/4| = 0.25, |0.75| = 0.75, |−1.5| = 1.5, |2| = 2. The number CLOSEST to zero — regardless of sign — is −1/4.
feedback: 0.75 is close to zero, but one of the negatives sits even closer. Compare distances, not signs.
−1.5 is the second-farthest from zero. Being negative does not make a number small in absolute value.
2 is the farthest of all — two whole units from zero.
hints: Rewrite each as a distance from zero: drop every sign first.
As decimals, the distances are 1.5, 0.75, 0.25, and 2.
The least distance wins. Which of 0.25, 0.75, 1.5, 2 is smallest?

steps: Problem: Complete the table for the integer 9: find its absolute value and its opposite.
Student's thinking: Absolute value and opposite both just make a number positive, so they should give the same answer as each other.
Student's answer: Absolute value of 9 = 9, and opposite of 9 = 9.
core.explanation: Absolute value and opposite are different operations. Absolute value measures distance from zero and is never negative: |9| = 9. Opposite reflects a number to the other side of zero, flipping its sign: the opposite of 9 is -9, not 9. The two operations only give the same result for the number 0 — every other number has a different absolute value and opposite.
hints: The opposite of a number always lands on the OTHER side of zero. Where is -9 compared to 9 on the number line?
Check the fill-table row for 4: its absolute value is 4, but its opposite is -4 — they are different! Now check the row for 9. Does the opposite of a positive number stay positive?

core.prompt: Three cities have temperatures of -12°F, -5°F, and 3°F. Which city is warmest?
core.explanation: 3°F is the greatest because it is farthest to the right on the number line. The order from coldest to warmest is -12, -5, 3.
feedback: Not quite. The order from coldest to warmest is -12, -5, ___.
This one is farthest to the left on the number line, which makes it the coldest reading rather than the warmest. Warmer temperatures sit farther right.
The three readings are different numbers, so they cannot describe the same temperature. Place them on a number line and compare their positions.
hints: Warmest = greatest temperature. On a thermometer, greater is higher — farther right on a number line.
Compare positions on a number line: temperatures farther right are warmer. Check where negatives sit versus positives.
Place -12, -5, and 3 on a number line and find the one farthest to the right. That city is warmest.

hints: Which number is farther to the left on the number line?

stretch.prompt: A submarine is at -150 meters and a bird is flying at +150 meters. A student says the submarine is closer to sea level because -150 is less than 150. Is the student correct? Explain using absolute value.
stretch.frame: The student is ___ because absolute value measures ___. Since |-150| = ___ and |150| = ___, both are ___ from sea level. The student confused ___ with ___.
stretch.explanation: The student is not correct. Absolute value measures distance from sea level, and |-150| = 150 while |150| = 150, so the submarine and the bird are exactly the same distance from 0. The comparison -150 < 150 describes position — below versus above sea level — not closeness to it.
hints: 'Closer to sea level' is about DISTANCE from 0, not about which number is less.
Compare |-150| and |150| — the distances. Then separately note that -150 < 150 is about position, not distance.
Start by finding |-150|: the submarine's distance from sea level in meters. Then find the bird's distance and compare.

steps: Problem: Compare -3 and -8. Which is greater?
Student thinking: 8 is bigger than 3, so -8 must be greater than -3
stretch.explanation: With negative numbers, the number closer to zero is GREATER. -3 is closer to zero than -8, so -3 > -8. The student compared the digits without considering that negatives work in the opposite direction.
hints: Plot -3 and -8 on a number line. Which one is farther to the right?
For negatives, closer to zero means greater. -3 is only 3 units from zero, but -8 is 8 units away.

stretch.prompt: A student says: 'Negative numbers are always less than positive numbers, so -100 is less than 1.' Is this correct? Now the student says: '-100 is less than -1 because 100 is greater than 1.' Is THIS correct? Explain the difference.
stretch.frame: The first statement is ___ because ___. The second statement is ___ because with negative numbers, ___. On the number line, -100 is ___ of -1, so ___.
stretch.explanation: The first statement is true: -100 is negative and 1 is positive, so -100 sits left of 1 on the number line and is less. The second answer, -100 < -1, is also true, but the reason given is wrong — it is not because 100 > 1, it is because -100 lies 100 units below zero while -1 lies only 1 unit below, putting -100 farther left.
hints: Two separate claims to judge — an answer can be right while the REASON is wrong. Check each on a number line.
For -100 vs -1, don't compare 100 and 1. Compare positions: which number sits farther below zero?
Place -100 and 1 first: negative vs positive settles claim 1. Then place -100 and -1 and see which is farther left.
